infra.kube.clusters.title: Kubeconfig on this machine
infra.kube.clusters.empty: The kubeconfig exists but declares no context yet.

infra.kube.col.name: Name
infra.kube.add.head: Add an EKS cluster
infra.kube.add.empty: Nothing searched yet — pick a profile and region, then Find clusters.
infra.kube.add.note: Equivalent command: aws eks update-kubeconfig --name <cluster> --region <region> --profile <profile>. No typing needed.
infra.kube.pods.rowHint: Click a row to see that pod its logs / description.
infra.kube.workloads.pickFirst: Pick a cluster in the bar above — every command below runs against that cluster.
infra.kube.act.logsWhy: Read this pod its logs (the output stays on your machine).
infra.kube.act.describeWhy: Read the full description of this pod (metadata, not secret contents).
infra.kube.act.deletePodWhy: The pod is deleted. If it belongs to a deployment, that deployment creates another one.
infra.kube.act.restartWhy: The pods of this deployment are recreated one at a time (rolling restart).
infra.kube.act.listNsWhy: List the namespace names of the cluster (names only, no data inside).
infra.kube.act.listPodsWhy: List pod names/status in the namespace (summary table, not object contents).
infra.kube.act.listDeploysWhy: List deployment names/status in the namespace (summary table).
infra.kube.act.containersWhy: Read the pod description to get container names for the log pane container picker.
infra.kube.act.findClustersWhy: Ask AWS for the EKS clusters in the selected profile and region (read only).
infra.kube.act.addClusterWhy: Write the cluster into ~/.kube/config so kubectl can use it. Nothing changes on the cluster.
infra.kube.act.exec: Open a shell in the pod
infra.kube.act.execWhy: Run kubectl exec -it to open an interactive shell inside this pod. From it you can run any command inside the container.
infra.kube.exec.unavailable: The terminal is unavailable (the engine bridge is not connected).
infra.kube.error.unreadable: The sidecar returned data we cannot read.
infra.kube.error.refresh: Could not load data from the cluster.
infra.kube.error.logs: Could not read this pod its logs.
infra.kube.error.describe: Could not read this pod its description.
infra.kube.error.clusters: Could not fetch the EKS cluster list.
infra.kube.error.addCluster: Could not add the cluster to your kubeconfig.
infra.kube.blocked.consequence: The permission matrix blocks this command. Copy it and run it yourself if you really mean to.
infra.kube.blocked.copyFailed: Could not write to the clipboard — select the command and copy it by hand.
infra.kube.log.capped: Drawing only the first {shown}/{total} matching lines.
infra.kube.report.title: Cluster report
infra.kube.report.sub: Computed from the kubectl tables just read (pods · deployments · nodes · CPU/memory · events). This is not an SLA and does not replace real monitoring.
infra.kube.report.lamp.warn: There is something worth a look
infra.kube.report.lamp.bad: A pod or deployment is not ready
infra.kube.report.noData: Nothing read from the cluster yet. Pick a cluster above and press ↻.
infra.kube.report.monitorCap: Stops itself after {min} minutes, and stops the moment you leave this view — no loop left running in the background.
infra.kube.report.copyFailed: Could not write the report to the clipboard.

infra.kube.report.md.head: # Cluster report {where}
infra.kube.report.md.restarts: - Restarts: {total} ({perPod} per pod, {recent} pods restarted recently)
infra.kube.report.detail.ok: Every running pod is ready and nothing has restarted.
infra.kube.footnote: The identity kubectl uses lives in the kubeconfig itself: a static token/certificate, or the exec plugin aws eks get-token (in that case AWOG passes the session its pinned profile into kubectl its environment). This screen is read-only until you press an action — and every command lands in the activity log.

infra.kube.act.listNodesWhy: Read the cluster node table (names, status, kubelet version — not object contents).
infra.kube.act.topWhy: Ask metrics-server for current CPU/memory use (numbers only, no application data).
infra.kube.act.capacityWhy: Read `kubectl describe nodes`: allocatable CPU/memory and how much of it pods have already reserved (requests). No object contents.
infra.kube.act.hpaWhy: Read the HorizontalPodAutoscaler table — current replicas, the min/max range and the metric each one targets.
infra.kube.act.inventoryWhy: Read the summary table of this kind (names and status only — not object contents).
infra.kube.act.eventsWhy: Read the Warning events of the namespace — this is where kubernetes says why a pod cannot start.
infra.kube.error.nodes: Could not read the node table.
infra.kube.error.top: Could not read CPU/memory. The cluster may not have metrics-server installed.
infra.kube.error.events: Could not read the events of this namespace.
infra.kube.error.capacity: Could not read node capacity (kubectl describe nodes).
infra.kube.error.hpa: Could not read the autoscaler table.
infra.kube.error.statefulsets: Could not read the StatefulSet table.
infra.kube.error.daemonsets: Could not read the DaemonSet table.
infra.kube.error.jobs: Could not read the Job table.
infra.kube.error.pvc: Could not read the volume claim table.
infra.kube.error.services: Could not read the Service table.
infra.kube.error.ingresses: Could not read the Ingress table.
infra.kube.report.refreshAll: Read all six tables again (pods, deployments, nodes, CPU/memory, events)
infra.kube.report.recentRestarts: {n} pods restarted in the last {min} min
infra.kube.report.eventsNone: No Warning events — the cluster has not complained in this scope.
infra.kube.report.eventsMore: and {n} more groups not shown here.
infra.kube.report.gap.nodes: Could not read the node table.
infra.kube.report.gap.top: No CPU/memory numbers. The cluster needs metrics-server for `kubectl top` to answer.
infra.kube.report.gap.events: Could not read the events of this namespace.
infra.kube.report.detail.nodes: {n} nodes are not ready ({list}) — the pods on them will follow.
infra.kube.report.detail.restartsRecent: {n} restarts, the newest {ago} ago on {top} — {recent} pods restarted in the last {min} min.
infra.kube.report.detail.tight: {n} nodes are tight (node {node}: CPU {cpu}, memory {mem}) — new pods may not fit.
infra.kube.report.detail.cordoned: {n} nodes take no new pods ({list}) — usually a drain in progress.
infra.kube.report.detail.versions: Nodes do not run the same kubelet version: {list}
infra.kube.report.detail.fresh: {n} pods came up in the last {min} minutes — something is changing.
infra.kube.report.md.usage: - Busiest node CPU/memory: {cpu} / {mem} · measured pod total: {cpuSum} / {memSum}
infra.kube.report.reservedTitle: Reserved by pod requests — the scheduler will not hand this share to anyone else, even while it sits idle.
infra.kube.report.hpaNone: No HorizontalPodAutoscaler here — replica counts are whatever was set by hand.
infra.kube.report.pvcNone: No PersistentVolumeClaims — nothing here keeps state on disk.
infra.kube.report.ingNone: No Ingresses — nothing is published through an ingress controller.
infra.kube.report.chartHealth: Score and the busiest node, over time
infra.kube.report.gap.capacity: No node capacity. `kubectl describe nodes` did not answer, so reserved CPU/memory is unknown.
infra.kube.report.gap.pvc: Could not read the volume claims.
infra.kube.report.detail.packed: {n} nodes have nearly all of their CPU/memory reserved (node {node}: CPU {cpu}, memory {mem}) — new pods will stay Pending even while the node looks idle.
infra.kube.report.detail.podSlots: {n} nodes are near their pod limit (node {node}: {used}/{cap}) — that cap is the kubelet's, not a resource shortage.
infra.kube.report.detail.hpaMax: {n} autoscalers are at their maximum ({list}) — they have no room left to scale out.
infra.kube.report.detail.hpaUnknown: Autoscalers with no metric to read: {list} — they are holding the replica count blind.
infra.kube.report.detail.workloads: {n} StatefulSets/DaemonSets/Jobs are not where they should be ({list}).
infra.kube.report.detail.pvc: {n} volume claims are not Bound ({list}) — the pods waiting on them cannot start.
infra.kube.report.detail.network: {n} Services/Ingresses have no address yet ({list}) — they exist but nothing can reach them.
infra.kube.report.md.workloads: - Other workloads: {n} StatefulSets/DaemonSets/Jobs, not where they should be: {bad}
infra.kube.report.md.storageNet: - Storage/network: {pvc} volume claims ({size}), {svc} Services, {ing} Ingresses, no address yet: {pending}
infra.kube.log.noneLeft: Every line was filtered out. Turn a level back on, or widen the time range.
infra.kube.report.impactClear: Nothing here is reaching users right now.
infra.kube.report.act.copyFailed: Could not write the command to the clipboard.
infra.kube.report.failPending: not scheduled onto any node yet
infra.kube.report.noRollout: No rollout in the last 24 hours.
infra.kube.report.endpointsNone: No Services in this namespace — nothing is reachable by name inside the cluster.
infra.kube.report.quotaNone: This namespace sets no quota — nothing will stop a deploy from taking the whole cluster.
infra.kube.report.pdbNone: No PodDisruptionBudget — a drain takes pods down with nothing to hold it back.
infra.kube.report.riskClear: Quota, autoscalers, disruption budgets and Service endpoints all have room.
infra.kube.report.eventsStaleOnly: {n} warnings, all older than {min} min — grouped away.

infra.kube.report.detail.quota: Namespace quota is nearly used up: {list}.
